recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No FHIR core source follow-up is needed for FHIR-19885; any future editorial harmonization of migrated THO CodeSystem metadata should be handled through THO/UTG.
issue_request: FHIR-19885 was Published with resolution Persuasive with Modification. It asked Patient Care to reduce unnecessary differences between condition-ver-status and allergyintolerance-verification value sets/code systems by removing the extra Codes wording from AllergyIntolerance names/titles, removing binding-strength wording from definitions, confirming the unconfirmed canonical status mapping, and preserving the incompatible URL differences.
initial_application: Jira comment GH#eb72252 points to git commit eb7225265a5055b6f9956367ea288e88c564e8a8, which changed the AllergyIntolerance verification value set and code system name, title, and description. The same Jira comment thread split the canonical unconfirmed status display concern into FHIR-20402 after the linked Zulip discussion identified it as a tooling/display issue.
additional_context: AllergyIntolerance and Condition are active resources in source/fhir.ini. Current core value set sources use AllergyIntoleranceVerificationStatus and ConditionVerificationStatus names, titles without the obsolete Codes suffix, and descriptions without binding-strength wording. source/status-codes.xml currently maps AllergyIntolerance.verificationStatus unconfirmed and Condition.verificationStatus unconfirmed/provisional to canonical unconfirmed. The historical CodeSystem XML files were later removed from core as THO duplicates, so further CodeSystem metadata edits would now belong to THO/UTG rather than this FHIR core checkout.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. No core source edit was needed because the active value set and status-code mapping sources already satisfy the accepted non-substantive alignment, and the URL change was explicitly rejected for compatibility.
